clue.text: Carol holds fruit by sticking a fork in

indicators.note: something that holds another thing has it inside, so the singing word wraps round the fruit

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A singer at Christmas clutches some fruit while eating it with a fork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is the verb, and 'holds' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearing something means piercing it with a pointed tool, as a diner does with a fork.

clue.text: A winger is seen in strip

indicators.note: the little word is seen inside the other piece, so it is placed within it

parts.note: to strip a fruit or animal is to skin it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with wings, perhaps a footballer, is spotted in their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A winger' suggests a footballer on the flank, but here it is a bird; 'seen in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small finch, a bird and so a creature with wings.

clue.text: Eve and, possibly, another woman

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Eve and maybe a second female figure, as if listing women of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the six letters of EVE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Evadne is a female name from Greek myth, the wife of Capaneus, so a woman other than Eve.

clue.text: Described crack journalist

parts.note: a crack is a sharp bang, also called a report, as from a gun
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A top-class reporter gave an account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack journalist' reads as an expert reporter, but 'crack' is the noun for a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reported something is to have given an account of it.

clue.text: An old ruler of generous heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so the letters come from the middle of generous

explanation.surface: A bygone monarch who was kind at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle four letters of 'generous' give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor of the first century.

clue.text: A town's ring road, complete

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
ST is short for street, a road
to complete something is to end it

explanation.surface: A town's ring road has been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Ostend is a Belgian port town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a coastal town in Belgium.

clue.text: Pay is to be raised unfortunately on the railway

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it
in a down clue, raising a word turns it upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Rail workers' wages are going up, more's the pity.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to be raised' turns the word upwards, and 'on' stacks it above the railway letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is the fixed payment an employee receives.

clue.text: An egg. &gin concoction is really delightful

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drink of egg and gin is said to be lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' mixes the letters of AN EGG and GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something engaging is charming and attractive, which a really delightful thing is.

clue.text: Gift for a fellow-a tin with nothing in it

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: with links the tin to what goes inside it
in it says the nought is placed inside the tin's letters

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A present for a man: an empty tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing in it' sounds like an empty tin, but it puts O inside TIN to give ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, especially money given to a cause.

clue.text: They photograph fish

explanation.surface: Some people take pictures of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappers is slang for press photographers, and the snapper is a sea fish.

clue.text: Bottle on the stone? Just the reverse!

indicators.note: the order is swapped, so instead of on before stone it is stone before on

parts.note: a flag is a flat paving stone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bottle sitting on a stone, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the stone' would put ON first; 'Just the reverse!' puts FLAG first.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or cider.

clue.text: This loaf is a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone declares this loaf of bread a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a British crusty loaf with diagonal slashes, and also slang for a blunder.

clue.text: Pass over devastated region

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Travel above a ruined area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass over' reads as flying above, but means take no notice of.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over someone is to disregard or overlook them.

clue.text: Quite satisfactory, so there's none left

explanation.surface: Things are fine, as nothing remains.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a joke: if every one is on the right, none is on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: All right means acceptable; read literally, everything on the right leaves nothing on the left.

clue.text: Capital place for tramp longing to get back

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily, to step

indicators.note: getting back means going in reverse, so the word for longing is read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: A London district suits a homeless wanderer who wants to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' looks like a vagrant but is the verb to walk; 'to get back' turns YEN into NEY. Stepney is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepney is a district in the East End of London, the capital.

clue.text: Part once it's all organised

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving three letters

explanation.surface: A role becomes available once everything is in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all organised' rearranges ONCE and ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is one part or division of a whole.

clue.text: Reverse for a French party

parts.note: un is French for a
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Turn things back for a French celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' is the definition, not a signal to turn letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to reverse its effect.

clue.text: He would" accept a quarrel caused distress

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: he would shortens to he'd
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: He'd take on an argument that upset people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarrel' looks like an argument but is the bolt shot from a crossbow; 'accept' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrowed means tormented or distressed; to have harrowed someone is to have upset them badly.

clue.text: Item to be read about family speculation

indicators.note: about means round, so the item word goes round the family word

parts.note: an item is a thing
kin are family

explanation.surface: A news story about a family is pure guesswork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'to be read' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking is reasoning about something, as speculation is.

clue.text: Music played these days in tranquil surroundings

indicators.note: the calm word surrounds the time word, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: serene means tranquil
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Modern tunes are performed in a peaceful setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' tells you the calm word goes round the era abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a piece of music played or sung, traditionally under a lover's window.

clue.text: Pain in the stomach, entirely due to stress

indicators.note: in signals letters lying inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A stomach pain caused only by stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'stomACH Entirely'; 'due to stress' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Rounds made by midshipmen here in a seagoing vessel

indicators.note: in places the middle letters inside the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a seagoing vessel
read as mid-shipmen, the middle letter of shipmen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Junior naval officers aboard ship produce round objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midshipmen' looks like naval cadets but splits as mid-shipmen, the middle letter of shipmen; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheres are round solid shapes, like balls or globes.

clue.text: Much like another large drink!

explanation.surface: A big drink that resembles the previous one.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a lookalike of someone, and also a twice-sized measure of spirits.

clue.text: Vet in a mess, as is natural

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An animal doctor in disarray, which is only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' jumbles VET IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Native means inborn or innate, the sense of natural.

clue.text: Dealing with coin lately issued

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with
a cent is a coin

explanation.surface: Handling money that was minted not long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: RE means 'concerning', as in a letter heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent means new or of late, as something just put out is.

clue.text: South African money, including some paid for freedom

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Currency from South Africa, part of it handed over to free a hostage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' is the container signal; the rand is South Africa's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransomed captive was released on payment of a sum demanded.

clue.text: A delegate deputy member scoffed

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: An envoy and an assistant member ate greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a committee member, but is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy or emissary, someone sent to act on another's behalf.

clue.text: For example a right back's passion

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: A full-back on the right shows great fervour, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right back' looks like the football position, but 'back' turns EG A R round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is violent anger, a passion in its older sense of strong feeling.

clue.text: Port — put a little by

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount
taken as written

explanation.surface: A harbour town, saving a small sum.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitby is a port on the Yorkshire coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitby is a fishing harbour town in North Yorkshire.

clue.text: A sponger's father tries a corrective

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: a corrective puts things into a different order, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A scrounger's dad attempts some discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrective' is the anagram signal, applied to the words 'tries a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off others without giving back, as a scrounger does.

clue.text: Some latitude is allowed for academic achievement

explanation.surface: A little leeway is permitted for a university qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is a measure of latitude or a measure of freedom, and also a university qualification.

clue.text: After ten meet, maybe about noon, to arrange accommodation

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the noon letter
maybe says the letters might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Once ten people meet around midday, lodgings must be sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns TEN MEET into TENEMET, and 'about' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building of rented flats, a form of housing.
